stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVES
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To compare the dose intensity and toxicity profiles for patients undergoing chemotherapy at the Townsville Cancer Centre (TCC), a tertiary cancer centre in northern Queensland, with those for patients treated in Mount Isa, supervised by the same medical oncologists via teleoncology.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: DESIGN
stage1_evidence_shown.context: A quasi-experimental design comparing two patient groups.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: SETTING
stage1_evidence_shown.context: TCC and Mount Isa Hospital, which both operate under the auspices of the Townsville Teleoncology Network (TTN).

stage1_evidence_shown.label: PARTICIPANTS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Eligible patients who received chemotherapy at TCC or Mt Isa Hospital between 1 May 2007 and 30 April 2012.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: INTERVENTION
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Teleoncology model for managing cancer patients in rural towns.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Dose intensity (doses, number of cycles and lines of treatment) and toxicity rates (rate of serious side effects, hospital admissions and mortality).

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"maybe","confidence":0.35,"reason_for_action":"The provided evidence describes a comparative study of teleoncology versus tertiary care measuring dose intensity and toxicity, but no results are given, so safety cannot be determined from this info."}

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: Over 5 years, 89 patients received a total of 626 cycles of various chemotherapy regimens in Mount Isa. During the same period, 117 patients who received a total of 799 cycles of chemotherapy at TCC were eligible for inclusion in the comparison group. There were no significant differences between the Mount Isa and TCC patients in most demographic characteristics, mean numbers of treatment cycles, dose intensities, proportions of side effects, and hospital admissions. There were no toxicity-related deaths in either group.
